dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows code people read, compare and copy — an example in its documentation, a command to run, a configuration file, a response from its API, a log — set apart from the text around it, in a face whose columns line up, on its page and inside its cards and panels, at the interface's size and smaller where room is short.

dev.tanrei.llm.usage: Everything a code block reads: for each look (filled, outlined) its fill; its corners and edge; for each size the code's text style and the padding around it; the code's color and tab width; the header's spacing and the styles of its title and language label; where the copy button sits; the line numbers', the prompt's and the line marks' colors and measures; for each of the nine syntax roles (comment, keyword, string, constant, function, type, tag, property, punctuation) its color and the weight it gains; and the longest code the block highlights by itself.
rules: The code block highlights by itself: give it the code and `language`. Do not write a highlighter, a theme or a stylesheet for code; a run you give yourself still wins over the block's own.

The syntax roles are an axis of this component. A system that needs another role (an operator, a decorator) adds a value to the axis under `vocabulary` and teaches its highlighter to name it; it does not restyle another role's runs.

Syntax has hues of its own, from palettes the system declares for it. Never give a syntax role a status color (error, success, warning, info), the link color or the focus color: in a code block success is an added line, error a removed line and primary the highlighted line, and nothing else.

Every syntax color must read on the block's fill, on the band of a highlighted line and on any surface an outlined block is placed on: the build holds each at 4.5:1 (7:1 in the high-contrast schemes).
A role changes a run's color and weight, nothing else: no slant, no underline, no background, no size.
Use filled on a page and outlined inside a container that is already filled. Inside a colored container (a callout) use filled, so the code reads on a surface.
Line numbers, the prompt and the line marks are drawn, never text: they are not selected and not copied.
Code is always left-to-right. In a right-to-left layout only the header and the copy button change sides.
Restyle through these tokens in a layer; never draw a code frame by hand.

color.$description: The filled look's fill: a quiet step off the page. Every text color of the block is read on it.
The outlined look's fill: none. The code is read on the surface the block is placed on.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: This look has no fill; the surface behind shows through.

padding-block.$description: Space above the first line and below the last, per size. Under a header the space above is header.padding-block-end in its place.

padding-inline.$description: Space before the start of a line (or of the gutter, where there is one) and after the end of the longest, per size; also the inset of the header's title.

color.$description: The outlined look's edge: the system's one hairline. Decorative: the face and the padding set the code apart without it.

width.$description: The width of the outlined look's edge, drawn inside the block's size. The filled look draws no edge.

typescale.$description: The code's text style, per size, taken whole: every line is one line of it high.

color.$description: The color of code that carries no syntax role, and of all code that is not highlighted.

tab-size.$description: How many columns of the code face a tab character advances to the next multiple of.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: A count of characters, not a distance: it scales with the code's own size, and no dial moves it.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows code written with tabs — a Makefile, Go, its users' own files — and decides once how deep an indent reads in its interface.
One product names what a block of code is — the file it belongs to, the language it is in — on the block itself, so a page of several blocks can be followed.

gap.$description: Space between the header's items: the title, the language and the copy button.

padding-block-end.$description: Space between the header's row and the first line of code.

typescale.$description: The title's text style. A product whose titles are always file names may set the small code role here.

color.$description: The language label's color: quieter than the title, which it may stand beside.

inset.$description: The distance of the copy button from the block's top edge and from its end edge. With the medium size's padding it centres a small button on the first line of code, so a block of one line holds the button without growing.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product places the copy control of its code tight in the corner or level with the first line, apart from how much room it gives the code itself.
One product refers to lines of code by number — in a review, in a tutorial's text, in an error it reports — and draws those numbers quieter than the code and apart from it.

color.$description: The line numbers' color. They are set in the code's own text style, with digits of one width.

gap.$description: Space between the gutter (the bar's column, the numbers and the signs) and the start of the code.

color.$description: The color of the prompt drawn before each line of a block of commands.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product documents commands to type and marks them with a prompt, quieter than the command, that is not part of what is typed or copied.
One product points at lines inside a block of code — the line its text talks about, the lines a change adds and the lines it takes away — without relying on color alone.

width.$description: The width of the bar drawn at the left edge of a highlighted, an added or a removed line.

color.$description: The band behind a highlighted line, from the block's left edge to its right. Decorative: the bar marks the line where the band cannot be seen (an outlined block on a surface of the same tone, forced colors).
The bar of a highlighted line: the color of the one that is chosen.
The bar and the plus sign of an added line.
The bar and the minus sign of a removed line.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product shows highlighted code and decides what each kind of word looks like once, for every language it shows and in every scheme: which kinds recede, which stand out by weight and which by color.

color.$description: The color of each syntax role. These are the values of a system that gives code no hue; the default system's layer values the chromatic roles from its syntax palettes.

comment.$description: Comments and documentation comments: what the code's author says about the code. Quieter than the code, and without a hue.

keyword.$description: The language's own words: keywords, storage and modifier words, at-rules, annotations. The code's color here, told by weight; the default system gives it a purple as well.

string.$description: Text written in the code: strings, characters, regular expressions, the values of markup attributes, the text of a template. The code's color here; the default system gives it a green, from a palette that is syntax's own and not the success color.

constant.$description: Values that are not text: numbers, booleans and null, named constants, units, color values, escapes. The code's color here; the default system gives it an orange.

function.$description: The name of a function or a method, where it is declared and where it is called. The code's color here; the default system gives it a blue.

type.$description: The name of a type: a class, a structure, an interface, an enumeration, a built-in type, a namespace. The code's color here; the default system gives it a blue-green.

tag.$description: What markup and style sheets address: an element's name, a component's name in markup, a selector. The code's color here; the default system gives it a red, from a palette that is syntax's own and not the error color.

property.$description: A name that belongs to something: a property, a key of an object or of a data file, an attribute of markup, a declaration's property in a style sheet, an option of a command. The code's color here; the default system gives it the blue of a function's name at a tone nearer the text.

punctuation.$description: Brackets, separators and the delimiters of markup: quieter than the words they hold together. Operators are not punctuation: they stay the code's color.

emphasis.$description: How much weight a run of each role gains over the weight of the code's text style. 0 draws the role at the code's weight.

dev.tanrei.vocabulary.rationale: One product tells kinds of words by weight, by color, or by both: a system with few hues leans on weight, and one with many draws every word at one weight.

dev.tanrei.derive.fixed: No weight is added: this role is told by its color or stays the code's own.

keyword.$description: Keywords gain the amount strong text gains in running text: they are told by weight before they are told by color, so they are still told where color is not seen.

string.$description: The weight a string gains: none.

max-length.$description: The longest code, in characters, that the block highlights by itself. Longer code is drawn plain: a run is a piece of the document on every platform, and a file of many thousands of lines is read in an editor, not in a page.
